span.label: mechanisms
span.term: weak ties bridge otherwise-separate communities, so removing them fragments the network via a percolation-like phase transition (a societal-scale confirmation of Granovetter strength-of-weak-ties)
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The reconstructed graph covers only mobile voice calls, not the full range of interactions between people.
span.note: what this limits: every claim about social ties from this graph: THE MCG CAPTURES ONLY A SUBSET OF ALL INTERACTIONS BETWEEN INDIVIDUALS, [excluding] FACE-TO-FACE, EMAIL AND LANDLINE
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The reciprocity requirement used to define a link may discard genuine social ties (false negatives).
span.note: what this limits: the link definition: the reciprocity requirement INDUCES SOME FALSE NEGATIVES, I.E. SOME LINKS CORRESPONDING TO GENUINE SOCIAL INTERACTION MAY GO UNDETECTED
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The data are a single-operator sample of the underlying national call network, not the whole population network.
span.note: what this limits: any population-level reading: ALTHOUGH THE DATASET COVERS SOME SEVEN MILLION USERS, IT IS NEVERTHELESS A SAMPLE OF THE UNDERLYING PHONE CALL NETWORK - scale is not coverage
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The strength of a social tie is measured as the total time two people spent on the phone.
span.note: what this limits: any claim here about the strength of social ties: strength is defined as the aggregated duration of calls between two users, after one-way calls have been eliminated by a reciprocity requirement
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The network studied is a stand-in for the communication network, and the paper says so.
span.note: what this limits: conclusions drawn here about human communication: the mobile call graph is used as a proxy for the communication network between users, being skewed toward trusted interactions because people share mobile numbers only with those they trust
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Three incompatible accounts of what drives tie strength were on the table before the measurement.
span.note: what this limits: the interpretation of the correlation reported here: the paper sets out a dyadic hypothesis, in which strength is independent of the surrounding network, against the strength of weak ties hypothesis, in which strength increases with friendship-circle overlap
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The conclusion sits between the positions rather than choosing one.
span.note: what this limits: the finding as support for any single theory of tie strength: the authors state it is in part driven by local network structure, in contrast with both a purely dyadic view and a global view
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: percolation and network analysis (robustness, phase transitions) applied to a society-scale communication network
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.note: eliminates: the network's TOPOLOGY as the explanation of the spreading result - the graph is held fixed and only the weights are flattened, so any difference must come from the distribution of tie strengths rather than from who is connected to whom

span.label: tie strength - AS AGGREGATED CALL DURATION: the sociological construct is measured by total air time between two people, over links that survive a reciprocity filter, so a strong tie here means many minutes and nothing else

span.label: what determines tie strength - THREE NAMED AND INCOMPATIBLE ANSWERS: a global efficiency principle in which strengths are optimised for overall flow, a dyadic hypothesis in which strength is independent of the surrounding network, and the strength of weak ties hypothesis in which it rises with friendship-circle overlap
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Analysing millions of mobile-phone users communication, tie strength couples with network topology: strong ties sit within communities, weak ties bridge them.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Counterintuitively, the social network is ROBUST to removing strong ties but falls apart via a phase transition when weak ties are removed — and this coupling slows information diffusion, trapping it in communities (Granovetter weak-ties hypothesis at scale).
